A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the UV sensitivity of phage T1, as measured by the plaque-forming efficiency, is determined by the UV sensitivity of the host cell and the UV sensitivity of a T1 gene product involved in the repair of the host cell DNA.
UV-irradiation of phage T1 results in a reduction of its plaque-forming ability (PF) in excision repair-proficient E. coli cells.
the T-even and T5 phage systems differ in their ability to utilize the host-cell repair machinery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
T5 infection inhibits the host-cell repair of UV-irra-diated DNA, probably at the level of incision.

the T-even phages have evolved a mechanism that allows them to repair their DNA after UV-irradiation, and that T5 has evolved a countermeat to this repair mechanism, which is effective in both excision repair proficient and -deficient hosts.

the inhibition of HCR by phage infection is not a general feature of all phage-host interactions but rather a special case of a specific phage-host relationship, which may have been selected during evolution to enhance the survival of T-even and T5 phages in a UV-irradiation environment.
